utterances.text: What was your status within the SDB? Was your reputation as that of a reliable or an unreliable person?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, I can only answer that indirectly, having in mind the issues discussed here, the intelligence part of politics, particularly when it comes to Kosovo and the international community. My reputation was of a high standing. Now, of course, they will say it was a very bad reputation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I wanted to show you an exhibit, it's 2D6.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have that on a screen. It is a book. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this was disclosed by the OTP under Rule 68. This book was mentioned on several occasions by the witness. It's called, "A Requiem for State Secret." We translated it in part, and as soon as a full translation is available, we'll hand it over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: A full translation of what? Not the whole book.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of this excerpt. It includes several pages of the book. Could we see page 2 of 9 in the English translation. In e-court that is page 5. I will read out a passage, and the Bench has that in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Mijatovic says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Fila please specify what paragraph he's reading from. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, the interpreters have a problem. They want to know where you're reading from, what page of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The book "Requiem for a State Secret," page 209 of the book in the Serbian. In e-court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So is that it, what we now. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: "We have connected Mr. Tanic as a liaison with the foreign intelligence agency before the multi-party system was established, and slowly started a little game, which was common on such occasions. In order to secure ourselves, we had acquired rather solid compromising material in time, in case unwanted events should occur in our operative combination. Even as a superintendent, I worked along with the operative that led him on creating compromising documentation, and in two instances, I personally paid Mr. Tanic for his effort... Tanic liked money, and as a result of that he had problems numerous times with the colleagues in the public security." That was the first quote. Did you have problems with the state -- with public security?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no problems with them. On several occasions they intended to submit criminal reports against me, and then it turned out they were all false, hence I had no problems with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Do you know Nenad Milic [Realtime transcript read in error "Lilic"]? He was the chef du cabinet to Zoran Djindjic and Mihajlovic's deputy in the party.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That person worked on such a case of a false criminal report, but it was rejected by the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Did he arrest you in 1996 and 1997 for illegal trade of chemical agents?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was a completely different case. We tried to collect a debt from a person, and that person submitted a criminal report. Nenad Milic did not arrest me but summoned me for an interview. I need to explain to the Court. And then the SDB intervened. They asked that this be done through regular channels and that it be sent to the court so that Milic wouldn't meddle with it. As soon as it reached the court, I submitted evidence and it was rejected.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't "Lilic" but "Milic" in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The next quote, the same page --

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nenad Milic, "M."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The same page, next quote: "More serious work with Tanic started when he relied on the English intelligence service ... He was regularly contacted by an English intelligence officer George Busby ... He had contacts with important people, and had created many friendly contacts, some of which he even recruited. Tanic was persuaded by the money, and he was not the only one." What is your comment? This is stated by your friend Zoran Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, he is to appear here and he will be examined by the OTP. It is not correct that they started working seriously with me when I started cooperating with the English intelligence service. The second sentence, I can comment in closed session because there are names mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Fila's microphone wasn't on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it wasn't protected for Mr. Mijatovic. Maybe this is his right -- proper name. As for the money and the persuasion, the best evidence, since I was given waiver by the British Security Service to speak openly, we worked in 1992 and 1993 against Milosevic's regime, to suppress his madness, and the first money I received was as late as 1999. Up until then, we even shared costs for lunch. Therefore, until 1999, I got nothing. Then I don't think I could be persuaded by money. There is proof that we even shared lunch costs. And I don't want to comment on the name of that person, because you don't know, Mr. Fila, whether that is his real name or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on. Page 6 in e-court, the next quote, Mijatovic is addressing Mr. Nice, and he says: "Tanic, during NATO bombing, tried to cheat on us. The then-head of the Belgrade centre was not operationally illiterate. He allowed for accounts to be settled between him and the service, and it was clear the way it was customary for such situations when agents are caught lying. And I wanted to tell Marina to tell Nice that the aforementioned person was spanked." This is Mijatovic's view of your abduction.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not in full, because a few pages later he addresses my abduction more seriously and in detail in the same book. Otherwise, this is incorrect, that I tried to lie to the security service during the war; otherwise, I would have been legally arrested for deception and I would have received a prolonged prison sentence. In any case, I wouldn't have been sent abroad and I couldn't have come back with the same result that Milic did and no one's saying that Milic lied. I would have been arrested had I lied, but what can you do you do? He'll be here as a witness. He'll have to wash his hands. It is completely incorrect as a description. I wasn't spanked. I would never ask anyone to be spanked the way I was. Perhaps we can leaf through some other pages where Mr. Mijatovic addresses my abduction in different terms.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Fila repeat the question because he overlapped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, would you start that question again because you overlapped with the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to ask whether the -- to elicit the witness's comment, and he provided one.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The next quote, Mr. Nice: "I am deputy head of the service. Mr. Mihajlovic is a former party comrade and former advisor of the Ministry of the Interior and he is afraid of coming back to the country. This is illogical, isn't it? And we looked into it and lo and behold, everything boils down to Mr. Busby. The preparation for Hague witness testimony is well underway. Mr. Tanic is loafing about the North American [as interpreted] continent and throughout Europe, and now he's enjoying the money to the hilt and this is the thing that he likes most." What does this mean, that you've been prepared by this person here, referred to as Busby, whichever name he may have, and to be prepared for your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the interpretation. I said Northern Europe continent, not the North American continent. I'd like this mistake to be rectified. Northern Europe is referred to, not North American. My comment would be the following: At the time when this was being prepared, the Hague Tribunal, the trial, the person referred to here as Busby - and I cannot confirm or deny that - was never here. I had never seen him before. You can see it from the transcripts. We had not met during that time. He had no preparations with me. To the contrary. They learned some things from me and this is why I was commented upon in Belgrade, and that he's -- I've explained his position of deputy head of service and Mihajlovic's position as Minister of the Interior. This was the reason why I never came back to Serbia. They were very dear to me, but it became clear to me that that person could not even return the stolen books from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Yes, this is your testimony already.

utterances.speaker: RATOMIR TANIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the person referred to as Busby had not met me at the time; this can be verified. He had no preparations with me and I had not changed my appearance. I haven't changed my acts, et cetera. I had not changed my actions because part of that was published in 1997 of what I had done -- of my contacts, and I wasn't strolling across Northern Europe. This can be verified by the Court. I just went to Paris once to see Petrovic and Mihajlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: I have two quotes and I'll be finished for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, Mr. Fila, we -- well, let's check whether there's another trial here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we can't go on. I know it's ridiculous, Mr. Fila, that we have to work in this way, but these questions and answers have a tendency to go on at great length and there's a couple of things that need to be clarified. You say that -- well, let me ask you the question this way. When did you meet Busby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the person referred to in this book as George Busby, I met him in 1992/1993 [as interpreted], in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the answer that's been transcribed is not very clear. Were -- are you saying that you didn't meet him around the time of giving your statement here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Absolutely. We spoke once, but we did not meet at that time in 1999/2000. I never met with the person. You may ask the Brits. And in no way did he influence my testimony, because he learned many things with regard to Serbian or Milosevic's secrets from me; the secrets about provoking the war and he learned many things from me to be able to ask ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Fila, how much more have you got in your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm at middle point, but I'm going to accelerate. I have two more quotes from the books, and I'll be wrapping up his intelligence career.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a problem with the interpretation. It says, "I never met this person." I meant I never saw that person in the period 1999/2000. We spoke on the phone once or twice, and that was all. And that person did not participate in priming me for testimony in the ICTY and no other secret service --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... We've got that information already. It's just repetition of what you've already told us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the cross-examination has already run for about the same length of time as the examination-in-chief, and that's roughly our touchstone. So what is the position?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will have to ask for more time, because we've lost quite a lot of time by the dragging of the witness's feet. And I've -- as you see, I will accelerate and it will be seen from my conduct that I don't want this to be prolonged and deferred, but he's a very important witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that you should have some discussion immediately after the Court rises and speak with the court deputy to give him some indication of what time-scale's involved here. And you probably should also consult with Mr. Hannis on that, because it -- it certainly will be of interest to me to know how long re-examination might be so that we can climb ahead. Mr. Tanic, that brings our session today to an end because another case has to come into this court, and we have to remove ourselves very quickly. Please leave the court with the usher, and bear in mind the instruction I gave you before that you must not discuss the evidence overnight with anyone. Back here to resume tomorrow at 9.00. Oh, yes, and we'll now go closed session while you leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 15th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
